Apple is reportedly developing a screenless health and fitness tracker to compete with Whoop, according to a new report from Bloomberg. The company is said to be "developing a prototype," but has yet to decide whether it will ultimately release the product.

The prototype reportedly being developed inside Apple features "a thin fabric band with a computing module containing sensors inside." The project is currently in the "technical exploration" phase, with Bloomberg noting that the product won't launch until 2028 at the earliest—if Apple decides to bring it to market at all.

The project is said to have the backing of Apple executives, including Eddy Cue and Tim Cook. Cue took the helm of Apple's health team after Jeff Williams departed last October.

Products like Whoop and the Oura Ring have proven popular among users who want to track health and fitness metrics without wearing a smartwatch. Oura is preparing for an initial public offering (IPO), according to Reuters, and recently disclosed that it sold 3.6 million Oura Rings over the 12-month period ending June 30; revenue grew 74% to $1.21 billion over the nine-month period ending June 30.

However, Apple remains the dominant player in the smartwatch market. The Apple Watch also offers a broader set of features than health-and-fitness-focused wearables like Oura and Whoop.
